title: CALM-TS: Risk-Controlled LLM Labeling for Time-Series via Calibrated Selective Gating

problem.claim: Time-series event labeling is expensive and subjective, while distribution drift causes label definitions to evolve over time.

gap.claim: LLM-generated weak labels can include natural-language rationales, but their error rates are unbounded and their failure modes are opaque.

contributions.claim: A risk-controlled weak-supervision pipeline that bounds labeling error while maximizing coverage.
Behavioral probing and a lightweight calibrator convert disagreement signals into risk-bounded acceptance with finite-sample guarantees.
Auditable evidence chains and a coverage-based, label-free drift indicator.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method reportedly reduces labeling cost by 77--81% on MIMIC-III and Yahoo~S5 at empirical risk ≤ a=0.05 across all 10 dataset-seed pairs.

On the PhysioNet Challenge 2015 binary alarm-verification task, the method reportedly achieves a 15.0% relative risk reduction over the unfiltered LLM at coverage 0.286 and is the only one of nine baselines with a lower five-seed mean risk at non-trivial coverage.

narrative_sequence.summary: Time-series labeling is costly, subjective, and affected by evolving label definitions under distribution drift.
LLM weak labels provide rationales but have unbounded error rates and opaque failure modes.
CALM-TS combines behavioral probing with calibration to selectively accept labels under finite-sample risk bounds.
The authors report cost and risk improvements across benchmark datasets and a challenge task.
The framework provides auditable evidence chains and a label-free drift indicator based on coverage.

source_observation.claim: Disagreement signals from prompt form, sampling temperature, and temporal context are calibrated into selective acceptance with finite-sample risk bounds.

interpretation.claim: Multiple behavioral perturbations may help identify uncertain weak labels before they are accepted.

application.claim: Use disagreement-aware selective gating when deploying LLM-generated labels in drifting time-series workflows.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that the approach generalizes beyond the reported datasets, task, or stated coverage and risk conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the calibrator algorithm or the exact finite-sample guarantee.
The abstract does not report labeling costs, coverage, or risk for every benchmark condition.
The abstract does not provide implementation, data-processing, or reproducibility details.
